newsitem.title: CHINA: Volkswagen Shanghai venture meets 1996 target.
newsitem.headline: Volkswagen Shanghai venture meets 1996 target.

text.p: A joint venture between Volkswagen AG and Shanghai Automobile Industrial Corp reached its 1996 production target of 200,000 Santana cars, the Liberation Daily reported on Sunday.
The joint venture produced 160,000 Santanas in 1995.
Santanas account for more than 50 percent of China's domestic car market, the newspaper said.
So far the joint venture had produced a total of 746,410 Santanas, including 104,378 of its newest model, the 2000 cc Santana, it said.
The local content rate of the 2000 cc model was 80 percent and of the earlier standard model 90 percent, it said.

The joint venture, established in 1985, has been the top foreign-invested joint venture in China for five consecutive years in terms of sales, with 1996 sales worth more than 20 billion yuan, it said but gave no more details.
Company officials said in October the firm had 15,000 cars in stock, higher than usual levels, because of over-supply and fierce competition in the domestic car market.
